(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.description: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) causes brief episodes of mild to intense dizziness triggered by specific changes in head position.
precautions: Avoid sudden head movements
Lie down in a calm, dim room during episodes
Perform Canalith repositioning (Epley maneuver)
Stay hydrated and avoid driving while dizzy

AIDS.description: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome is a chronic condition caused by HIV that weakens the immune system and impairs the body's ability to fight infection.
precautions: Adhere strictly to Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)
Practice safe sex and barrier protection
Maintain strict hygiene and food safety
Avoid contact with infectious individuals

Acne.description: A skin condition that occurs when hair follicles plug with oil and dead skin cells, causing whiteheads, blackheads, or pimples.
precautions: Wash face twice daily with mild cleanser
Avoid popping or squeezing lesions
Use non-comedogenic cosmetics
Limit high-glycemic foods and excess dairy

Alcoholic hepatitis.description: Liver inflammation caused by chronic and heavy alcohol consumption, leading to liver cell damage and jaundice.
precautions: Stop alcohol consumption completely
Consume a nutrient-dense, high-protein diet
Monitor liver function and jaundice levels
Seek addiction counseling and medical detox support

Allergy.description: An immune system reaction to a foreign substance (allergen) such as pollen, pet dander, dust mites, or certain foods.
precautions: Identify and avoid specific allergen triggers
Use over-the-counter or prescribed antihistamines
Keep living spaces clean and well-ventilated
Carry an epinephrine auto-injector if severe

Arthritis.description: Inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain, swelling, and stiffness that can worsen with age.
precautions: Engage in low-impact physical therapy and swimming
Maintain a healthy weight to reduce joint load
Apply alternating warm and cold compresses
Take prescribed anti-inflammatory medication

Bronchial Asthma.description: A chronic condition in which airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus, making breathing difficult.
precautions: Always carry a rescue inhaler
Avoid cold air, dust, smoke, and pollen triggers
Monitor peak flow breathing rates
Practice breathing exercises and maintain clean air

Cervical spondylosis.description: Age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in your neck, leading to chronic stiffness and radiating pain.
precautions: Maintain ergonomic posture when using screens
Perform gentle neck stretching exercises daily
Use an orthopedic supportive pillow
Avoid carrying heavy loads on shoulders

Chicken pox.description: A highly contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus, characterized by an itchy, blister-like rash.
precautions: Isolate from uninfected individuals until all blisters crust
Apply calamine lotion to soothe itching
Trim fingernails to prevent secondary skin infections
Rest and drink plenty of fluids

Chronic cholestasis.description: A condition where bile flow from the liver is reduced or stalled for an extended duration, causing pruritus and jaundice.
precautions: Follow a low-fat, balanced diet
Supplement with fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
Avoid hepatotoxic medications and alcohol
Regular liver enzyme blood panels

Common Cold.description: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract primarily affecting the nose, throat, sinuses, and larynx.
precautions: Rest adequately and drink warm fluids
Use saline nasal drops and steam inhalation
Gargle with warm salt water
Wash hands frequently to avoid spreading

Dengue.description: A mosquito-borne viral disease that occurs in tropical and subtropical areas, causing high fever, severe headache, and joint pain.
precautions: Monitor platelet counts daily via CBC tests
Maintain aggressive oral hydration (ORS, coconut water)
Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen (use paracetamol only)
Prevent mosquito bites and eliminate standing water

Diabetes.description: A metabolic disorder that causes high blood sugar due to insufficient insulin production or cellular insulin resistance.
precautions: Monitor blood glucose levels regularly
Adopt a low-glycemic, fiber-rich diet
Engage in at least 30 minutes of daily exercise
Inspect feet daily for sores or loss of sensation

Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).description: Swollen and inflamed veins in the lower rectum and anus, causing rectal bleeding, pain, and itching.
precautions: Eat high-fiber foods and drink plenty of water
Avoid straining during bowel movements
Take warm sitz baths for 15-20 minutes
Avoid prolonged sitting on the toilet

Drug Reaction.description: An adverse reaction or allergy to a specific pharmaceutical drug, presenting as skin eruptions, hives, or systemic symptoms.
precautions: Immediately discontinue the suspected drug under medical guidance
Seek emergency care if lip/throat swelling occurs
Record drug allergy on medical profile
Take prescribed antihistamines or corticosteroids

Fungal infection.description: An infection caused by fungus affecting the skin, nails, or hair (such as ringworm, tinea, or athlete's foot).
precautions: Keep affected skin clean, dry, and cool
Apply topical antifungal creams as prescribed
Do not share towels, clothes, or personal items
Wear loose-fitting, breathable cotton clothing

GERD.description: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease occurs when stomach acid repeatedly flows back into the esophagus, irritating the lining.
precautions: Avoid spicy, acidic, fatty, and caffeinated foods
Do not lie down within 3 hours after eating
Elevate the head of your bed by 6-9 inches
Eat smaller, more frequent meals

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract involving the stomach and small intestine, causing diarrhea, cramps, and nausea.
precautions: Drink Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) frequently
Eat bland foods following the BRAT diet (bananas, rice, applesauce, toast)
Avoid dairy, alcohol, and spicy foods
Practice thorough handwashing

Heart attack.description: A medical emergency occurring when blood flow to a part of the heart muscle is severely reduced or blocked.
precautions: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (911/112) IMMEDIATELY
Chew an aspirin if recommended by emergency dispatch
Remain seated and calm, loosen tight clothing
Begin CPR if the individual becomes unresponsive

Hepatitis B.description: A serious liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmitted through infected blood or bodily fluids.
precautions: Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic substances
Vaccinate close household contacts
Do not share needles, razors, or toothbrushes
Follow viral load and liver function tests regularly

Hepatitis C.description: A blood-borne viral infection that causes inflammation of the liver, leading to chronic liver damage if untreated.
precautions: Consult a specialist for direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy
Avoid alcohol and smoking completely
Maintain healthy nutrition and weight
Avoid sharing items that may carry blood traces

Hepatitis D.description: A rare and severe liver infection caused by the hepatitis D virus (HDV) that only occurs in people infected with hepatitis B.
precautions: Maintain antiviral medication regimen
Strict avoidance of alcohol
Monitor liver fibrosis and cirrhosis biomarkers
Adhere to barrier precautions

Hepatitis E.description: A liver disease caused by the hepatitis E virus (HEV), commonly transmitted through contaminated drinking water.
precautions: Drink only boiled or filtered purified water
Practice strict food hygiene and avoid raw shellfish
Ensure plenty of bed rest and fluid intake
Pregnant women must seek immediate medical attention

Hypertension.description: A chronic medical condition in which the blood pressure in the arteries is persistently elevated above 130/80 mmHg.
precautions: Reduce dietary sodium intake (<2g/day)
Exercise regularly for at least 30 minutes daily
Avoid smoking and limit alcohol intake
Monitor blood pressure at home and take medications as prescribed

Hyperthyroidism.description: A condition where the thyroid gland produces excess thyroid hormones, causing rapid heart rate, weight loss, and nervousness.
precautions: Take antithyroid medications as directed
Avoid excess dietary iodine and kelp
Practice stress management techniques
Monitor resting heart rate and thyroid panel

Hypoglycemia.description: A deficiency of glucose in the bloodstream, leading to shaking, sweating, confusion, and dizziness.
precautions: Consume 15-20g fast-acting carbohydrates immediately (e.g. juice, glucose tablets)
Re-check blood glucose after 15 minutes (Rule of 15)
Carry portable sugar snacks at all times
Adjust diabetic medication dosage under doctor guidance

Hypothyroidism.description: An underactive thyroid gland that does not produce enough thyroid hormones, leading to fatigue, weight gain, and cold sensitivity.
precautions: Take levothyroxine medication on an empty stomach 30-60 min before breakfast
Have regular TSH and free T4 blood tests
Maintain a balanced, nutrient-rich diet
Exercise to boost metabolism and energy levels

Impetigo.description: A highly contagious bacterial skin infection that mainly affects infants and young children, causing sores around nose and mouth.
precautions: Wash sores gently with antibacterial soap and warm water
Apply prescribed antibiotic ointment and cover lightly with gauze
Wash hands, bedding, and clothes in hot water
Do not touch or scratch the crusts

Jaundice.description: A yellowing of the skin and eyes caused by high bilirubin levels, indicating liver, gallbladder, or red blood cell issues.
precautions: Undergo immediate liver function and ultrasound tests
Drink fresh water and stay well hydrated
Avoid fatty, oily, and heavy foods
Completely abstain from alcohol

Malaria.description: A mosquito-borne infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, characterized by cyclic fever, chills, and sweats.
precautions: Complete the full course of prescribed antimalarial medication (ACT)
Use insecticide-treated bed nets and repellent
Maintain adequate fluid intake and rest
Seek emergency care if confusion or severe vomiting occurs

Migraine.description: A neurological condition causing intense, debilitating throbbing headache pain, often accompanied by nausea and light sensitivity.
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark, and cool room
Identify and avoid triggers (aged cheese, stress, lack of sleep)
Stay well-hydrated throughout the day
Take acute migraine relief medications at early onset

Osteoarthristis.description: The most common form of arthritis, caused by the breakdown of protective cartilage cushioning the ends of bones.
precautions: Engage in low-impact aerobic exercise (walking, swimming)
Maintain a healthy body weight to protect knee and hip joints
Apply thermal therapy (heat pads or ice packs)
Use assistive devices if needed to maintain mobility

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).description: Loss of muscle function and movement resulting from bleeding in the brain tissue (hemorrhagic stroke).
precautions: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY (FAST protocol)
Strict blood pressure control under intensive care
Engage in dedicated neuro-rehabilitation and physical therapy
Prevent falls and aspiration

Peptic ulcer diseae.description: Painful sores on the lining of the stomach, small intestine, or esophagus caused by acid erosion or H. pylori bacteria.
precautions: Avoid NSAID painkillers like ibuprofen and aspirin
Take proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) as prescribed
Limit caffeine, acidic drinks, and spicy foods
Eat meals on a regular schedule

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus, causing cough and fever.
precautions: Take the full course of prescribed antibiotics or antivirals
Get plenty of rest and drink lots of fluids
Use a humidifier or inhale warm steam
Seek emergency care if breathing becomes labored or lips turn blue

Psoriasis.description: A chronic autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the growth cycle of skin cells, leading to scaly, silvery plaques.
precautions: Moisturize skin daily with thick emollient ointments
Avoid skin injury, harsh soaps, and sunburn
Manage stress through relaxation techniques
Use prescribed topical corticosteroids or phototherapy

Tuberculosis.description: A potentially serious infectious bacterial disease that mainly affects the lungs, spread through microscopic respiratory droplets.
precautions: Strictly complete the 6-month DOTS antibiotic treatment
Wear a mask and ensure good room ventilation during infectious phase
Cover mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing
Maintain a high-protein, nourishing diet

Typhoid.description: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, transmitted through contaminated food or water, causing sustained high fever.
precautions: Complete the entire course of prescribed antibiotics
Drink only boiled or bottled water
Eat hot, freshly cooked foods; peel raw fruits yourself
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before eating

Urinary tract infection.description: An infection in any part of the urinary system (kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra), causing burning urination and urgency.
precautions: Drink plenty of water to flush bacteria from the urinary tract
Urinate as soon as the urge arises without holding it
Wipe from front to back after using the bathroom
Complete the prescribed antibiotic treatment course

Varicose veins.description: Gnarled, enlarged veins, most commonly appearing in the legs and feet due to weakened or damaged vein valves.
precautions: Wear graduated compression stockings
Elevate legs above heart level several times a day
Exercise regularly to improve circulation
Avoid standing or sitting in one place for long periods

hepatitis A.description: A highly contagious, short-term liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus (HAV), typically spread through contaminated food/water.
precautions: Rest adequately and stay hydrated
Avoid alcohol and medications metabolized by the liver
Practice strict handwashing before food preparation
Get vaccinated if not previously immunized
